analysis.investment_thesis: Excelsoft clears the earnings yield hurdle (~14% EBIT/EV using stated EV/EBITDA of 5.98), but ROCE of 16.4% falls short of the Magic Formula's 20% threshold, making this a mediocre-quality business at a decent-but-not-cheap price. The 2025 net profit spike is partly driven by a one-time Other Income jump (INR 2→15 Cr), masking a weaker underlying earnings trend.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at 17.7% CAGR (2020–25), a good top-line trajectory for a niche education SaaS player
Debt reduction is disciplined: borrowings slashed from INR 168 Cr (2020) to INR 45 Cr (2025), improving balance sheet quality
Operating CF positive all 5 years (INR 53–63 Cr range), demonstrating genuine cash conversion despite lumpy profits
key_risks: ROCE of 16.4% is sub-threshold; EBITDA CAGR of only 8.1% over 5 years signals margin erosion as revenue scales
Earnings quality concern: INR 15 Cr Other Income in FY25 (vs. INR 2 Cr norm) inflates reported net profit of INR 35 Cr — core earnings closer to INR 22–25 Cr
Tiny market cap (INR 812 Cr), highly niche (ed-tech SaaS in India), limited institutional interest (FII 1.4%, DII 4.1%) — liquidity and re-rating risk
red_flags: FY25 Free Cash Flow of INR 290 Cr is anomalous vs. OCF of INR 53 Cr and capex of INR 17 Cr — unreconciled gap suggests a large asset sale or investment liquidation not explained in the data
Net profit history is highly volatile: -5 → 11 → 15 → 22 → 13 → 35 Cr; forward P/E of 13x implies a near-doubling of earnings that has not yet been demonstrated operationally
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: using the stated EV/EBITDA of 5.98 and FY25 EBITDA of INR 87 Cr, implied EV ≈ INR 520 Cr. With EBIT (Operating Income) of INR 73 Cr, Earnings Yield = 73/520 ≈ 14% — this clears the 12% attractiveness threshold. However, Return on Capital (ROCE as reported) is 16.4%, which sits below the 20%+ bar the Magic Formula demands for a "good business." A company that ranks well on earnings yield but poorly on ROIC is, at best, a cigar butt — cheap but not compounding. Excelsoft doesn't even qualify as fully cheap given the EV discrepancy versus the stated market cap (INR 812 Cr + net debt implies EV ~839 Cr, not ~520 Cr), suggesting substantial off-balance-sheet investments or liquid assets that need verification.

The business fundamentals are mixed. Revenue growth at 17.7% CAGR is encouraging, and the debt paydown story is real and positive (finance costs fell from INR 13 Cr to INR 5 Cr). But operating margins have been range-bound (19–30%) and EBITDA has actually contracted in CAGR terms (8.1%), meaning operating leverage is absent. The FY25 "earnings beat" is partly manufactured by INR 15 Cr of Other Income (vs. a normal INR 2 Cr), and the anomalous INR 290 Cr FCF figure warrants deeper scrutiny. For the Magic Formula, this is a weak double: earnings yield is borderline acceptable, ROIC is below threshold, and earnings quality is suspect. I'd pass unless the EV/Other Income anomaly resolves in favour of the bull case.
